components.name: Control (default)
components.description: The press-button used for filters trigger, pagination, 'Copy brief,' and 'mark all read.' One of four distinct control chromes on the board (see .seg, .field, .toggle).
components.css: .ds-ctl { font-family: 'Hanken Grotesk', ui-sans-serif, system-ui, sans-serif; font-size: 0.8125rem; font-weight: 600; color: #4a5057; background: #fcfcfa; border: 1px solid #c7c7bf; border-radius: 3px; padding: 0.3125rem 0.625rem; line-height: 1.2; transition: border-color 120ms ease, color 120ms ease, background-color 120ms ease; } .ds-ctl:hover { border-color: #6b7178; color: #14161a; } .ds-ctl:focus-visible { outline: 2px solid #c22f16; outline-offset: 2px; border-radius: 2px; }

components.name: Control (active)
components.description: The active/selected state of the press-button (open filter sheet, current pagination page, 'Done' in the filter sheet).
components.css: .ds-ctl-active { font-family: 'Hanken Grotesk', ui-sans-serif, system-ui, sans-serif; font-size: 0.8125rem; font-weight: 600; color: #fcfcfa; background: #14161a; border: 1px solid #14161a; border-radius: 3px; padding: 0.3125rem 0.625rem; } .ds-ctl-active:focus-visible { outline: 2px solid #c22f16; outline-offset: 2px; border-radius: 2px; }

components.name: Segmented Control
components.description: One connected strip for a closed, mutually-exclusive choice (date range). A 2-column grid variant (.seg-grid) exists for narrow rails where a single row would wrap labels mid-word.
components.css: .ds-seg { display: inline-flex; border: 1px solid #c7c7bf; border-radius: 3px; background: #fcfcfa; overflow: hidden; } .ds-seg button { font-family: 'Hanken Grotesk', ui-sans-serif, system-ui, sans-serif; font-size: 0.8125rem; font-weight: 600; color: #4a5057; background: transparent; padding: 0.3125rem 0.625rem; border: none; border-right: 1px solid #c7c7bf; transition: background-color 120ms ease, color 120ms ease; } .ds-seg button:last-child { border-right: none; } .ds-seg button:hover { background: #f2f2ee; color: #14161a; } .ds-seg button[data-active='true'] { background: #14161a; color: #fcfcfa; }

components.name: Dropdown Field
components.description: Filled, recessed chrome for a 'choose from a list' control (company/topic/source/tag multi-select), distinct from the press-button's outlined chrome.
components.html: <button class="ds-field" aria-haspopup="listbox">Company <svg width="9" height="9" viewBox="0 0 12 12" fill="none"><path d="M3 4.5L6 7.5L9 4.5" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="1.5"/></svg></button>
components.css: .ds-field { display: inline-flex; align-items: center; justify-content: space-between; gap: 0.375rem; font-family: 'Hanken Grotesk', ui-sans-serif, system-ui, sans-serif; font-size: 0.8125rem; font-weight: 600; color: #4a5057; background: #f2f2ee; border: 1px solid transparent; border-radius: 3px; padding: 0.3125rem 0.625rem; line-height: 1.2; transition: background-color 120ms ease, border-color 120ms ease, color 120ms ease; } .ds-field:hover { background: #e8e8e2; } .ds-field[data-active='true'] { background: #e8eefb; border-color: #2f5fb8; color: #234a92; } .ds-field:focus-visible { outline: 2px solid #c22f16; outline-offset: 2px; border-radius: 2px; }

components.name: Toggle Switch
components.description: A true pill switch affordance for a binary state ('High signal only'), not a button standing in for two labels.
components.css: .ds-toggle { position: relative; display: inline-flex; align-items: center; width: 2rem; height: 1.125rem; border-radius: 999px; background: #c7c7bf; border: none; padding: 2px; transition: background-color 120ms ease; } .ds-toggle[data-active='true'] { background: #c22f16; } .ds-toggle::after { content: ''; display: block; width: 0.875rem; height: 0.875rem; border-radius: 999px; background: #fcfcfa; transition: transform 120ms ease; } .ds-toggle[data-active='true']::after { transform: translateX(0.875rem); }

components.name: Lane Chip
components.description: Small filled-square marker plus uppercase label; marks lane/status meaning ('Lead' in signal red, 'Also in the brief' in lane blue, 'Must read'). Replaces any colored-border-left device.
components.css: .ds-chip { display: inline-flex; align-items: center; gap: 0.375rem; font-family: 'Hanken Grotesk', ui-sans-serif, system-ui, sans-serif; font-size: 0.75rem; font-weight: 700; letter-spacing: 0.03em; text-transform: uppercase; } .ds-chip::before { content: ''; display: block; width: 0.5rem; height: 0.5rem; border-radius: 2px; background: currentColor; }

components.name: Active Filter Chip
components.description: Removable active-filter pill built on the field's active (lane) chrome, with a drawn-SVG remove icon.

components.name: Search Field
components.description: Icon-prefixed search input with its own recessed chrome, never a bordered box among buttons.
components.css: .ds-search { width: 100%; font-family: 'Hanken Grotesk', ui-sans-serif, system-ui, sans-serif; font-size: 0.8125rem; color: #14161a; background: #f2f2ee; border: 1px solid transparent; border-radius: 3px; padding: 0.375rem 0.625rem 0.375rem 2rem; transition: background-color 120ms ease, border-color 120ms ease; } .ds-search:hover { background: #e8e8e2; } .ds-search:focus { background: #fcfcfa; border-color: #c7c7bf; } .ds-search::placeholder { color: #6b7178; }

components.name: Board Panel Header
components.description: Flat colour-field (.band) section header used for lane headers, 'Companies in range,' and 'Strongest pairs' — grouping by filled band, not by boxing the whole cluster.

components.css: .ds-story { border-bottom: 1px solid #e2e2dc; list-style: none; } .ds-story-link { display: block; padding: 1rem 0; text-decoration: none; color: inherit; transition: background-color 120ms ease; } .ds-story-link:hover { background: #f2f2ee; } .ds-story-meta-row { display: flex; flex-wrap: wrap; align-items: center; gap: 0.625rem; } .ds-meter { display: inline-flex; align-items: center; gap: 2px; } .ds-bar { display: block; width: 3px; } .ds-label { font-family: 'Hanken Grotesk', ui-sans-serif, system-ui, sans-serif; font-size: 0.8125rem; font-weight: 500; color: #6b7178; } .ds-story-title { margin-top: 0.5rem; font-family: 'Hanken Grotesk', ui-sans-serif, system-ui, sans-serif; font-weight: 700; font-size: 1.4375rem; line-height: 1.16; color: #14161a; text-decoration-color: #c22f16; text-underline-offset: 6px; } .ds-story-link:hover .ds-story-title { text-decoration: underline; text-decoration-thickness: 2px; } .ds-story-summary { margin-top: 0.5rem; font-size: 1rem; line-height: 1.5; color: #4a5057; max-width: 68ch; } .ds-story-footer { margin-top: 0.5rem; display: flex; flex-wrap: wrap; align-items: center; gap: 0.75rem 0.375rem; } .ds-data { font-family: 'JetBrains Mono', ui-monospace, monospace; font-size: 0.75rem; color: #6b7178; font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums; } .ds-rule { height: 12px; width: 1px; background: #e2e2dc; }

narrative.overview:
Daybreak triages today's AI/tech news the way an operations board triages anything under active management: priority lanes, status colour, a compact status readout, and a working surface sized to use the room it has — not a page that hides the board behind a masthead. The system is abstracted deliberately per an explicit steer against theatricality: there is no literal aviation texture, iconography, or motif anywhere in the build. What survived the abstraction is the discipline underneath the metaphor — a Lead lane and a secondary lane, two functional accent colours reserved for status/priority, a flat colour-field band that does real grouping work, and distinct control chrome per control role — not the metaphor's surface dressing.

The palette is bright near-white (#fcfcfa), not the grey chart-paper or warm cream this category defaults to — it reads as a tool lit for desk work, not a printed page. Two functional accents carry meaning: signal red for importance/must-read/active-state, and a second blue 'lane' tone for the secondary-priority lane and for filter-active chrome. Everything else is ink and structural neutrals. One grotesk family, Hanken Grotesk, carries both display and UI type — a deliberate rejection of the prior build's three-typeface, editorial-versus-UI split — because a tool should read as one voice throughout, not a masthead layered over a UI kit. JetBrains Mono is reserved strictly for data that needs to line up in a column.

The board uses the full canvas: a 12-column desktop grid puts a control rail, the story lanes, and a companies-in-range panel in view together, collapsing to one column with a bottom filter sheet on mobile. Structure comes from two devices working together — hairline rules between rows, and flat .band colour fields for section headers — rather than either device alone. The system carries one confirmed defect forward rather than concealing it: the TopBar's two-row layout (wordmark+status on row one, full-width nav on row two) exists because a single combined row crushed nav labels to a single letter at mobile widths under real content pressure; it is documented here as the working pattern that fixed a real bug, not retconned as an aesthetic choice.
keyCharacteristics: Bright near-white ground (#fcfcfa), near-black ink, two functional accents (signal red, lane blue), each reserved for one job
One grotesk voice (Hanken Grotesk) for display and UI; JetBrains Mono reserved for tabular data only
A full-width, real multi-column desktop board (control rail | story lanes | companies panel) instead of a centered reading column
Distinct control chrome per role — press-button, segmented control, filled dropdown field, toggle switch, search field — never one button shape standing in for five behaviors
Flat colour-field .band headers plus hairline rules as the two structural devices, replacing colored-border-left cards
Small filled-square .chip markers (never a colored left-border) mark lane and status meaning

rules.name: The Two-Signal Rule
rules.body: Signal red and Lane blue each carry exactly one status meaning — importance/must-read/active-state for Signal, secondary-priority/filter-active for Lane — and never swap jobs or double as decoration. A third accent, or either color appearing outside these roles, dilutes the coding a status board depends on.

rules.name: The Chip-Not-Border Rule
rules.body: Lane and status meaning is marked with a small filled-square .chip marker plus label, never a colored left-border on a row or card. A colored-border-left device is the one thing this system explicitly does not use to encode priority.

rules.name: The One Voice Rule
rules.body: Display and UI type are the same family (Hanken Grotesk) at different weights, not two typefaces standing in for 'editorial' versus 'product.' A new surface should never reach for a second display face.

rules.name: The Real-Jump Rule
rules.body: Type-scale steps differ by meaningful amounts (12/13/16/19/23/30/40px), never a near-invisible 1-2px increment.

rules.name: The Flat-By-Default Rule
rules.body: Story rows, the overview band, and the control rail carry zero shadow. Only a surface that overlaps content it floats above — a popover or tooltip — earns the one shadow token.

dos: Do reserve signal red for importance-5/must-read/active-state only, and lane blue for secondary-lane/filter-active state only — each accent keeps exactly one job.
Do mark lane/status meaning with a small filled-square .chip plus label, never a colored left-border on a row or card.

Do give each control role its own chrome — press-button (.ctl), segmented control (.seg/.seg-grid), filled dropdown field (.field), toggle switch (.toggle), search field — instead of reusing one button shape for every interaction.
Do group sections with a flat .band colour field or a rule hairline, not a bordered/shadowed card.
Do let a board surface use the full max-w-[100rem] frame; reserve the narrower max-w-[65rem] reading column for long-form pages like How It Works.
Do keep the TopBar's two-row split (identity+status / full-width nav) on any new top-level nav — it fixed a real mobile label-crushing bug, not a stylistic preference.

Do hand-sync any hardcoded chart color/font constant (Analysis.tsx's INK/SIGNAL/LANE/SERIES) with --color-* whenever a token changes; SVG chart fills cannot read CSS custom properties reliably across export/print.
Do draw interface icons (remove, chevron, search) as inline SVG using currentColor; never set an icon as a unicode text glyph.
donts: Don't introduce a colored left-border on a card or row to encode status or priority — that device was explicitly replaced by the .chip filled-square marker.

Don't add literal aviation texture, iconography, or theming (strip-board graphics, radar/runway motifs, ATC-styled labels) anywhere in the interface — the metaphor was deliberately abstracted away per an explicit steer against theatricality; the shipped discipline is priority lanes and status colour, not decoration referencing the source metaphor.
Don't reach for a second display typeface. Hanken Grotesk carries both display and UI roles; JetBrains Mono is for tabular data only.
Don't use rule-2 for text; it is border-only by design. Use ink-3 as the contrast floor for text.
Don't add a third functional accent color, or let signal/lane double as decoration or a general brand color.
Don't collapse the desktop board back into a single centered reading column outside How It Works; the 12-column control-rail/lanes/panel grid is the system's spatial model for board-type views.
